title: "SQL adherence"

```{python}
import pandas as pd
from _common import ORDER, SHORT, jsonl, table, usd

RUN = "2026-11-02-sql-adherence"
s = jsonl(RUN, "samples.jsonl")
sm = jsonl(RUN, "summary.jsonl")
rp = jsonl(RUN, "repairs.jsonl")
dg = jsonl(RUN, "diagnosis.jsonl")
off = jsonl(RUN, "json_cut_offline.jsonl")
run_date = pd.to_datetime(s.created, utc=True).min().tz_convert("America/Vancouver").date()
GRID = ["baseline", "instructions", "json", "pydantic", "cut", "rewrite", "cut+pydantic", "json+pydantic",
        "json+cut+pydantic", "repair", "all", "all-instructions", "all-json", "all-pydantic", "all-repair"]
q = lambda v, m, col: sm[(sm.variant == v) & (sm.model == m)].iloc[0][col]
qw = "qwen/qwen3.8-27b"
```

Why does Qwen's SQL fail to run, and what fixes it? Fix in code what code can fix safely, and spend a model call only on what is left. **cut** keeps the reply's SQL up to the first semicolon that ends a complete statement (sqlglot finds it, so a `;` inside a string survives) and never rewrites the query. **pydantic** checks the SQL (one SELECT, known columns, DuckDB's EXPLAIN) and sends its error back for one retry. **json** is the provider's strict JSON-schema mode. 12 questions x 3 epochs per model and variant.

## Cut + validator against validator alone, Qwen 3.8 27B

::: {.caveat}
We run each eval block once. A block has several tests, but a proper statistical comparison needs several independent runs of every variant and a paired comparison on the same questions, reported with a confidence interval rather than a single percentage.
:::

```{python}
rows = []
for v in ["json+pydantic", "json+cut+pydantic", "pydantic", "cut+pydantic"]:
    rows.append({"variant": v, "SQL errors": f"{q(v, qw, 'SQL error rate'):.0%}",
                 "value correct": f"{q(v, qw, 'value-correct rate'):.0%}", "cuts": int(q(v, qw, "repairs applied")),
                 "retries (model calls)": int(q(v, qw, "retries used")), "price, 36 answers": usd(q(v, qw, "cost USD"), 4),
                 "median latency": f"{q(v, qw, 'median latency s')} s"})
oq = off[off.model == qw]
from IPython.display import Markdown
Markdown(pd.DataFrame(rows).to_markdown(index=False, colalign=["left"] + ["right"] * 6) + "\n\n: n = 36 answers per row: 12 questions, 3 times each")
```


With strict JSON mode on, Qwen often ends a correct query with the end of the JSON (`;"}`, `;,`). The cut removes it in code, so the validator sends `{python} int(q("json+cut+pydantic", qw, "retries used"))` retries instead of `{python} int(q("json+pydantic", qw, "retries used"))`, for `{python} f"{1 - q('json+cut+pydantic', qw, 'cost USD') / q('json+pydantic', qw, 'cost USD'):.0%}"` less. Every cut answer passed. When JSON mode is off, Qwen does not write that junk, so the cut finds nothing to do. Cut alone on the json run's replies: `{python} int(oq.cut.sum())` cuts, SQL errors `{python} f"{(oq.outcome_json == 'SQL error').mean():.0%}"` → `{python} f"{(oq.outcome_after_cut == 'SQL error').mean():.0%}"`. GPT-5.4 nano and mini: 0% SQL errors with the validator, in every variant.

## Full grid: SQL errors / correct / price

```{python}
#| output: asis
heads = " | ".join(f"{SHORT[m]}: SQL err / correct / price" for m in ORDER)
print(f"| variant | {heads} |\n|---|" + "---:|" * len(ORDER))
for v in GRID:
    cells = [f"{q(v, m, 'SQL error rate'):.0%} / {q(v, m, 'value-correct rate'):.0%} / {usd(q(v, m, 'cost USD'), 3)}" for m in ORDER]
    print(f"| {v} | " + " | ".join(cells) + " |")
```

On Qwen, strict JSON-schema mode raises SQL errors from `{python} f"{q('baseline', qw, 'SQL error rate'):.0%}"` to `{python} f"{q('json', qw, 'SQL error rate'):.0%}"`: it keeps the reply's shape and lets the end of the JSON leak into the `sql` string. *repair*, *all* and *all-…* ran the first post-processing (a plain split at `;` plus rewrite), *rewrite* is transpile and near-miss columns alone. *all* is instructions, json, pydantic and repair.
:::

## One failure, traced

```{python}
import json, re
def sql_of(text):
    m = re.match(r"^```(?:json)?\s*(.*?)\s*```$", text.strip(), re.S)
    return json.loads(m.group(1) if m else text)["sql"]
r = s[(s.model == qw) & (s.config == "pydantic") & (s.id == "q08") & (s.epoch == 2)].iloc[0]
```

q08 "`{python} r.question`" on Qwen, pydantic. The first reply makes 2 temp tables before its SELECT. The validator answers: *`{python} r.validation_error.removeprefix("sql: ")`*. The retry sends one SELECT, and DuckDB returns `{python} f"{r.value:.2f}"`, the reference.
:::
::::

```{python}
bad = rp[rp.changed_value | rp.wrong_after_repair]
safe = rp[rp.steps.map(lambda x: x == ["cut"]) & ~rp.variant.str.contains("repair|all")]
rw = rp[rp.variant == "rewrite"]
legacy_bad = bad[bad.variant.str.contains("repair|all")]
cut_wrong = rp[(rp.variant == "all") & (rp.id == "q08") & (rp.epoch == 2)].iloc[0]
```

**Post-processing, case by case** (every change is in `repairs.jsonl`). The sqlglot cut: `{python} len(safe)` answers cut, `{python} int((safe.outcome == "pass").sum())` of them then correct, none changed in meaning. Rewrite: `{python} len(rw)` answers, `{python} int((rw.outcome == "pass").sum())` then correct. It quotes a reserved alias (`JOIN zones do` becomes `JOIN zones AS "do"`). The first post-processing, with its plain split at `;`, ran `{python} len(legacy_bad)` repaired answers to a wrong value. In q08 it dropped a stray ` 0`, and a wrong query that would have failed returned `{python} f"{cut_wrong.value_after:.0f}"` against `{python} f"{cut_wrong.reference:.2f}"`: an error became a confident wrong number.

**Not tried:** GEPA prompt optimization in DSPy, set aside on purpose: it needs its own held-out training questions (a later lecture or a project option).
